name: the maximum edge count of a graph admitting no

phase_0.boundary_condition: the extremal function f(n) = max{|E(G)| : |V(G)|=n and every two cycles in G share at least one edge}
phase_0.domain_name: the maximum edge count of a graph admitting no
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: forward construction of candidate graphs by adding edges while preserving the no-edge-disjoint-cycles property, or advancing into the lower-bound enumeration
AFWD.justification: directed morphism that moves from an empty lower bound toward a concrete extremal example or a new case in the proof.

AREV.chosen_element: backtracking from a failed construction or contradictory assumption to a safe state, or retracting a case in the upper bound proof
AREV.justification: contravariant reversal that discards an invalid configuration and returns to a previous stable point.

CLINK.chosen_element: sequential composition of the isomorphism filter and the property checker for each graph
CLINK.justification: composition that chains the self-recognition test with the edge-disjoint-cycles decision, forming a single compound check.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: a borderline graph whose cycle detection yields both presence and absence of edge-disjoint cycles simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: the dialetheia arm: when the cycle retrieval algorithm produces inconsistent outputs on the same structure, both truth values are held without resolution, contributing B to the fused verdict.

EVALF.chosen_element: the state where no two edge-disjoint cycles exist
EVALF.justification: negative arm—the graph obeys the condition, so its edge count e becomes constructive proof that the maximum is at least e (T).

EVALT.chosen_element: the state where two edge-disjoint cycles are detected
EVALT.justification: affirmative arm of the property test—the graph violates the necessary condition and becomes an invalid witness, contributing nothing (N) to the lower bound.

FFUSE.chosen_element: fusion of all per-graph lower-bound contributions into the global maximum candidate, and later fusion of the lower and upper bounds
FFUSE.justification: the arms rejoin to a single state—contradictory evidence, such as a graph yielding both valid and invalid signals, fuses to B; overall the arcs amalgamate to the supremum of viable edge counts.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: branching on whether a graph contains two edge-disjoint cycles
FSPLIT.justification: the definitional condition forks the graph space: those possessing a forbidden pair of cycles and those obeying the restriction; multiple arms also open for enumeration and case analysis.

IFIX.chosen_element: the final extremal number (or the statement specifying its open status) permanently recorded in the corpus index
IFIX.justification: irreversible append-only fixation; once determined, the result cannot be retracted, becoming immutable canonical knowledge.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: isomorphism self-recognition: a labeled graph recognizing itself among previously examined isomorphism classes
IMSCRIB.justification: identity operation that prevents double-counting; if the graph is a duplicate, the check yields the neutral identity and contributes no new evidence.

TANCH.chosen_element: the final, sealed extremal theorem or open problem statement
TANCH.justification: terminal anchor that closes the investigation, containing the resolved f(n) and bounding the system under the Erdős corpus.

VINIT.chosen_element: the void before any graph or bound is established
VINIT.justification: initial state where the problem is posed but no candidate graph, edge count, or bound has been introduced; a purely uninitialized register.

phase_2.fuse_element: the per-graph contribution toward the extremal lower bound
phase_2.fuse_result: a single value: if valid and not contradictory, the statement 'f(n) ≥ e' holds (T); if contradictory, the statement carries B; otherwise N. This does not recreate the original graph.
phase_2.rejoin_note: Arm A contributes nothing; arm B contributes the edge count e; arm C contributes B. The arms rejoin to the maximum lower-bound evidence from this graph. The outer fusion later combines all graph arms into the global lower bound L.
phase_2.split_input: a single labeled graph G on n vertices
split_outputs: arm A: G contains two edge-disjoint cycles (invalid)
arm B: G does not contain two edge-disjoint cycles (valid)
arm C: both states held at once due to detection inconsistency (ambiguous)
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: contradictory evidence, such as a limit-case graph that simultaneously appears to avoid and contain edge-disjoint cycles, or lower and upper bounds that conflict before resolution; the paraconsistent result is the legitimate output.
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: an assumed upper bound is disproven by a counterexample, or a candidate graph is shown to possess a forbidden pair.
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: a specific n-vertex graph with e edges and no two edge-disjoint cycles exists, so the maximum is at least e.
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: no graph has been examined; the extremal number is unknown, register empty.

steps.domain_action: The extremal problem is posed in an uninitialized void; no graph, edge count, or bound is present.
The investigation bifurcates into two complementary arms: a lower-bound construction arm and an upper-bound proof arm.
Advance into the lower-bound arm; initialize the current maximum lower bound L to 0 and prepare graph enumeration.
The set of all labeled n-vertex graphs is split into parallel arms, one for each graph G.
For each G, sequentially compose an isomorphism self-check with the property decision.
Test whether G is isomorphic to a graph already examined; if it is a duplicate, the identity recognition yields the neutral state and no new evidence is generated.
Branch on the property P(G): does G contain two edge-disjoint cycles?
P(G) holds — a forbidden pair of cycles is found. The graph is rejected and contributes nothing (N).
P(G) fails — no such pair exists. The graph is a valid witness; its edge count e asserts that f(n) ≥ e (T).
The cycle detection algorithm returns conflicting signals for this graph, simultaneously asserting the presence and absence of edge-disjoint cycles; this arm contributes a live contradiction (B).
The three property arms (invalid, valid, ambiguous) rejoin into a single contribution for G: either N, T (e), or B.
All graph arms fuse; the supremum of the edge counts where T or B was contributed yields the global lower bound L. Conflicting B-states are preserved.
Complete the lower-bound arm and reverse to the top-level fork to enter the upper-bound arm.
Advance into the upper-bound arm; assume, for contradiction, that there exists an n-vertex graph H with edge count > K (a candidate upper bound) and no two edge-disjoint cycles.
Split the structural analysis of H into cases based on maximum degree Δ.
Case 1: Δ ≥ 3. Construct two edge-disjoint cycles using the high-degree vertex and the cycle space, reaching a contradiction.
The contradiction is realized; the assumption is false (F).
Descend to Case 2: Δ ≤ 2. The graph is a disjoint union of paths and cycles.
Further split Case 2 into subcases: H contains a long cycle, only triangles, etc.
In each subcase, derive an upper bound on edges that falls below K, confirming no counterexample can exist (F).
Fuse the subcase arms; all yield F, sealing the contradiction for the Δ ≤ 2 case.
Fuse the two case arms; the assumption is refuted, establishing an unconditional upper bound U = K.
The upper-bound proof is complete; return to the top-level fork.

The lower-bound arm (L) and the upper-bound arm (U) rejoin. If L = U the verdict is T (exact extremal number); if L < U the verdict is T with an unresolved gap; if contradictions force L > U the verdict is B (paraconsistent outcome).
The final verdict, together with the extremal function and any open range or B-state, is written irreversibly into the Erdős corpus index.
The boundary closes; the extremal edge count for graphs without two edge-disjoint cycles is now a sealed entry in the corpus.

phase_5.alfs_store: the Erdős corpus index as the immutable bootstrap store of extremal results and open problems
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the graph generation procedure that enumerates all labeled n-vertex graphs in order of increasing edge count, feeding them to the property checker
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the shared state register holding the current maximum lower bound L and the upper bound candidate K, accessible by both arms
phase_5.memory_mechanism: a canonical list of isomorphism class representatives and their property statuses, stored as a hash-indexed table
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: depth-first generation of graphs with pruning when an edge addition would certainly create edge-disjoint cycles

phase_6.cycle_cost: one complete cycle of enumerating all n-vertex graphs, testing the edge-disjoint-cycles property, and fusing the bounds
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the transformation from an open question to a resolved extremal function is entropy-conservative; all information is reorganized into the proof structure and the permanent record without net loss.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: the extremal number f(n) determined, or a precise gap with a paraconsistent status recorded
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the set of all labeled graphs on n vertices, no bound known
